lesson_title: The Invention That Fixed Everything: From Barter to Industry
hook_text: Ten thousand years of economics happened on one hillside. Watch.
clip_script: One village, long ago. Every family does everything — grows, sews, builds, carves. Nobody trades, because nobody has EXTRA. Then someone masters farming, and one year there's more than the family can eat. Extra changes everything: the clever-handed son stops farming and makes pots ALL DAY — and now he needs the farmer, and the farmer needs him. Specialists must trade. First they swap — and swapping is misery: hunt for the exact person who wants pots AND has grain; try paying half a goat; argue every price from scratch; watch your wealth rot or walk off. Four miseries. Then one market day, the village agrees: these iron pieces count as payment for ANYTHING. Watch four miseries die in an afternoon. Sell to anyone. Split any payment. Price everything on one measuring stick. And wealth can finally WAIT. That's money — half a trade, holdable. Roads follow. Rules follow. The chief arrives to tax and build. Then the machines come... and the village becomes the world you live in.
visual_style: A single hillside village evolving in continuous timelapse: huts to market square to roads to mill town, four misery-icons shattering as iron pieces glow, ending on a modern skyline grown from the same hill.
pacing: Story-teller cadence accelerating through the inventions, wide-shot finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and walk all ten thousand years in one sitting.
